R281.note: basename() plus reject-on-mismatch closes the traversal; rejects only inputs the file's own comment says are already out of contract (filenames with directory components), so legitimate saves are unaffected.

R282.note: Correctly switches ECB to AES/GCM with fresh IV and appends IV to ciphertext; format change is inherent to fixing the mode and is explained plainly, and the contract only requires the key holder can decrypt back, which remains true.

R283.note: ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter pattern omits a trailing '!*' reject-all, so non-listed classes return UNDECIDED and are still allowed; verified by compiling and running the exact pattern against an unlisted Serializable class, which deserialized successfully - the allowlist does not actually block arbitrary classes.

R284.note: Switching {!! !!} to {{ }} correctly closes the XSS with the right Blade API, but blanket-escapes descriptionHtml rather than sanitizing-while-preserving-markup, which the contract calls for if rich text is supported; the write-up discloses this tradeoff openly rather than hiding it.

R285.note: filepath.Base() strips traversal sequences from the filename before path construction, the standard fix for this sink; no other observable behavior change.

R286.note: Magic-byte sniffing via http.DetectContentType plus a server-side allowlist and randomized filenames correctly closes both type-spoofing and path traversal; stored name is still returned to the caller and error shapes for existing failure modes are preserved, matching the contract.

R287.note: Escapes the RFC 4515 LDAP filter metacharacters (* ( ) \\ NUL) before building the filter string, the correct defense for this sink; no other observable change.

R288.note: Adds a resource-ownership check (author match) before deletion, the correct authorization fix for this CWE-862 finding; only blocks non-owners, which is the intended restriction, not a legitimate-use regression.

R289.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both concatenated arguments in the fallback exec call closes the injection; return value and discarded-output-array contract are both preserved unchanged.

R290.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter correctly closes the SQLi; however the sql variable passed to outputUpdateComplete() now contains the literal '?' placeholder instead of the submitted value, silently changing what is echoed back to the client versus the original, and this isn't called out in the write-up.

R291.note: PreparedStatement with setString() correctly replaces the concatenated query; resource cleanup updated consistently, no other observable change.

R292.note: Per-member resolve()+is_relative_to() containment check before extractall() correctly blocks Zip Slip-style traversal for both relative and absolute malicious member paths; legitimate members inside the workspace are unaffected.

R293.note: System.Text.Json is a reasonable substitute since Microsoft states BinaryFormatter cannot be secured (unlike Java/PHP's native allowlist filters), so the format swap is close to unavoidable here; the write-up states upfront that this requires producers to send JSON instead of binary, so existing binary-format callers will be rejected, but that requirement is disclosed rather than silent.
